parts.title: Multiple choice (Questions 1–50)
parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

source.document: raw/2018_Science__V-A.pdf (7 pages: cover + questions on pp. 2-7, 'The End' after Q50)
source.notes: Cover: 'End-of-Basic Education (Grade 8) National Examination, Eritrea, 2018 – 4. Science – Version A'. Only Version A is available. Text from the PDF text layer, checked against the page images. Figures cropped at 250 dpi: barrel and ramp (Q25), food chain (Q35), incomplete circuit with gap X (Q42), land/sea breeze at night (Q47). Tables in Q22, Q39 and Q50 and the pie-chart key of Q30 are typed as stem tables. THREE DRAWINGS ARE MISSING FROM THE PDF ITSELF (checked with pdfimages and a vector-drawing scan; only their text labels are on the page): Q8 (plant cell and animal cell with part X), Q16 (stick in a beaker of water), Q30 (pie chart of air). Q16 and Q30 can still be answered from the text (Q30 has a printed key); Q8 cannot be answered with certainty.
source.printing_note: Clean digital print, but the Q8, Q16 and Q30 drawings did not survive into the PDF. Q16 label 'Beake r'; Q35 label 'Green plans' and the sun drawn as 'Su'; Q26 option A 'condom' is not a disease (the item still works: A is the answer). Kept as printed.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: Meter is the SI unit of
explanation_steps: The metre (m) is the SI unit of length.
Mass is in kilograms, time in seconds, and temperature in kelvin. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 8)
questions.explain_simple: We measure length in metres.
tips: SI: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time).

similar_questions.stem: Which is the SI unit of mass?
explanation_steps: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a liquid metal at room temperature?
explanation_steps: Mercury is a metal, but it is a silvery liquid at room temperature.
Iron, copper and gold are solid metals. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 36)
questions.explain_simple: Mercury is the metal that is liquid at room temperature.
tips: Mercury (Hg): liquid metal, used in some thermometers.

similar_questions.stem: The chemical symbol of mercury is
explanation_steps: Mercury's symbol is Hg (from its Latin name).

questions.stem: Friction is an example of
explanation_steps: Friction is a force that acts against motion when two surfaces rub together.
It is not matter (not a substance, solid or gas). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 28)
questions.explain_simple: Friction is a force. It slows moving things.
tips: Friction = force between surfaces that rub.

similar_questions.stem: Which makes friction smaller?
explanation_steps: Oil makes surfaces slippery, so friction becomes smaller.

questions.stem: The type of teeth with sharp edges used for biting and cutting solid foods are
explanation_steps: Incisors are the front teeth with sharp edges. They bite and cut food.
Canines tear, premolars and molars grind. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 6)
questions.explain_simple: Incisors, the front teeth, cut food.
tips: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind.

similar_questions.stem: Which teeth grind and crush food at the back of the mouth?
explanation_steps: Molars are at the back. They grind and crush food.

questions.stem: The type of energy produced by a burning candle is
explanation_steps: The wax of a candle stores chemical energy.
When the candle burns, this chemical energy changes into light energy (and heat).
The textbook gives 'the flame of a candle' as an example of light energy. Chemical energy is what the candle has before burning. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: A burning candle gives light. Its chemical energy changes to light and heat.
tips: Burning: chemical energy → heat + light.

similar_questions.stem: A torch battery stores
explanation_steps: A battery stores chemical energy and changes it to electrical energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a chemical change?
explanation_steps: A chemical change makes new substances.
Burning paper makes ash, smoke and gases. These are new substances.
Cutting, folding and dropping do not make anything new. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 47)
questions.explain_simple: Burning makes new substances. So it is a chemical change.
tips: New substance → chemical change.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a chemical change?
explanation_steps: Rust is a new substance, so rusting is a chemical change.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is used to kill germs in drinking water?
explanation_steps: The textbook says a chemical called chlorine can be used to kill micro-organisms (germs) in water.
Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Chlorine is added to water to kill germs.
tips: Safe water: boil it, or add chlorine.

similar_questions.stem: Another simple way to kill germs in drinking water at home is
explanation_steps: Boiling water kills most germs.

questions.stem: The diagram below represents two cells. Letter ‘X’ represent a part of each cell. Which part of the cell is labeled ‘X’ in both diagrams?
explanation_steps: NOTE: The drawing of the two cells is missing in the exam PDF. Only the labels 'X', 'Plant cell' and 'Animal cell' are printed.
X must be a part that both a plant cell and an animal cell have. That rules out the cell wall (only plant cells have it).
The usual part labelled in both cells in this kind of item is the nucleus. The answer is keyed C, but please check it against a printed paper.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 104)
questions.explain_simple: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus. The picture is missing, so check with your teacher.
tips: Both cells: nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane. Plant only: cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole.

similar_questions.stem: Which part is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
explanation_steps: Only plant cells have a cell wall.

textbook_ref.topic: 7.1 The cell – basic unit of life
textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Structure and Function in Living Things
textbook_ref.section: 7.1 The cell – basic unit of life

questions.review_flag: Figure missing: the two cell drawings are not in the PDF (only the labels X, 'Plant cell' and 'Animal cell' are printed). The answer cannot be read from the paper. Keyed C (nucleus), the usual shared part in this item. B (cell membrane) and D (cytoplasm) are also parts of both cells, so a teacher must check a printed copy.

questions.stem: The forces on an object with a net force of zero are called
explanation_steps: When the forces on an object are balanced, the net force is zero.
Velocity and acceleration are not forces. Unbalanced forces have a net force that is not zero. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 49)
questions.explain_simple: If the net force is zero, the forces are balanced.
tips: Net force 0 → balanced. Not 0 → unbalanced.

similar_questions.stem: A book lies still on a table. The forces on it are

options.C: zero because there are no forces

explanation_steps: Gravity pulls down and the table pushes up equally, so the forces are balanced.

questions.stem: Which of the following are artificial satellites?
explanation_steps: Artificial satellites are made by people. Examples: weather, communication, military and navigation satellites.
The moon and planets are natural satellites. Only option C has two artificial satellites. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 156; Science Grade 8, p. 155)
questions.explain_simple: Weather and military satellites are made by people. They are artificial.
tips: Natural: moon, planets. Artificial: made by people.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a natural satellite?
explanation_steps: The moon was not made by people. It is a natural satellite.

questions.stem: The lowest layer of the atmosphere is
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere.'
Above it are the stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The troposphere is the lowest layer. We live in it.
tips: From the ground up: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.

similar_questions.stem: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
explanation_steps: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

questions.stem: Filtration is a method of

options.A: removing solid particles from water using clean cloth
options.C: throwing rubbish into clean water using clean cloth
options.D: boiling clean water to kill micro-organisms

explanation_steps: Filtration passes dirty water through a filter (clean cloth, sand, stones). The solid particles stay in the filter.
Adding chemicals is chlorination; boiling kills germs. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 179)
questions.explain_simple: Filtration takes out solid bits by passing water through a cloth or sand.
tips: Filter = something with tiny holes that stops solids.

similar_questions.stem: Letting muddy water stand so that mud sinks, then pouring off the clean water, is called
explanation_steps: Settling and pouring off the water is decanting.

questions.stem: A cyclist travels at an average speed of 20 m/s to his friend’s house 5 km away. How long does it take the cyclist to make the distance?
explanation_steps: First change km to m: 5 km = 5000 m.
Time = distance ÷ speed = 5000 m ÷ 20 m/s = 250 s. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 55)
tips: time = distance ÷ speed. Change km to m first (1 km = 1000 m).

similar_questions.stem: A car moves at 10 m/s. How long does it take to go 2 km?

questions.stem: During water cycle, the process of cloud formation is known as
explanation_steps: Water vapour rises and cools. It changes from gas to tiny liquid drops. This forms clouds.
The textbook calls this process condensation. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Clouds form when water vapour cools and condenses.
tips: Evaporation → condensation (clouds) → precipitation (rain).

similar_questions.stem: Rain, snow and hail falling from clouds are called
explanation_steps: Water falling from clouds is precipitation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a male sex characteristic?

options.C: release of an egg from the ovary

explanation_steps: At puberty the voice box of a boy gets larger and his voice becomes deeper.
Larger breasts, release of eggs and menstruation are female characteristics. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 24)
questions.explain_simple: A deeper voice is a change in boys at puberty.
tips: Boys: deeper voice, beard, sperm. Girls: breasts, eggs, menstruation.

similar_questions.stem: Which change happens in girls at puberty?
explanation_steps: Menstruation starts in girls at puberty.

questions.stem: The diagram below represents a long stick in a glass of water. The stick’s broken appearance is caused by light that is
explanation_steps: When light passes from water into air, it bends. This bending is called refraction.
Because the light bends at the water surface, the stick looks bent or broken. Answer: A.
(The drawing of the stick is missing in the exam PDF, but the question can be answered from the words.)
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 74-75)
questions.explain_simple: Light bends when it leaves water. So the stick looks broken. This is refraction.
tips: Refraction = bending of light between two media.

similar_questions.stem: A swimming pool looks less deep than it really is because of
explanation_steps: Light bends as it leaves the water (refraction), so the bottom looks higher.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an element?
explanation_steps: An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances. Oxygen is an element.
Water, sugar and salt are compounds made of two or more elements. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 36)
questions.explain_simple: Oxygen is an element. Water, sugar and salt are compounds.
tips: Element = one kind of atom (O, C, Fe). Compound = two or more elements joined.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a compound?
explanation_steps: Carbon dioxide is made of carbon and oxygen joined together.

questions.stem: When a woman lifts a heavy box and moves it 10 m, she does a 200 J of work. Calculate the force applied by the woman?
explanation_steps: Work = force × distance, so force = work ÷ distance.
Force = 200 J ÷ 10 m = 20 N. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 59)
questions.explain_simple: Force = work ÷ distance = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 N.
tips: W = F × S → F = W ÷ S.

similar_questions.stem: A boy does 150 J of work pushing a cart with a force of 30 N. How far does the cart move?
explanation_steps: Distance = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 m.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true about function of human skeletal system?

options.A: supports the body and gives shape

explanation_steps: The skeleton supports the body, gives it shape, protects organs, and stores minerals like calcium and phosphorus.
Supplying oxygen is done by the respiratory and circulatory systems, not the skeleton. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 29; Science Grade 8, p. 33)
questions.explain_simple: The skeleton does not give oxygen. The lungs and blood do that.
tips: Skeleton: support, shape, protection, movement, stores minerals, makes blood cells.

similar_questions.stem: Which bone protects the brain?
explanation_steps: The skull protects the brain.

questions.stem: What does the pair of gene ‘TT’ represent?
explanation_steps: T is the gene for tall (dominant). Two same genes make a homozygous pair.
TT = homozygous tall, tt = homozygous short, Tt = heterozygous tall. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 136)
questions.explain_simple: TT has two tall genes that are the same. It is homozygous tall.
tips: Same letters = homozygous. Different letters (Tt) = heterozygous.

similar_questions.stem: A pea plant has the genes Tt. It is
explanation_steps: Tt has two different genes, and T (tall) is dominant.

questions.stem: The type of cell division meiosis occurs in
explanation_steps: The textbook says meiosis occurs only in the testes (to form sperms) and in the ovaries (to form eggs), or in flowers.
Skin, muscle and blood cells are body cells. They divide by mitosis. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Meiosis makes sex cells like sperm.
tips: Meiosis → sex cells. Mitosis → body cells.

similar_questions.stem: How many chromosomes does a sex cell have compared with a body cell?
explanation_steps: Meiosis halves the number of chromosomes.

questions.stem: The table below shows the function of some organs found in a human body system. Which human body system performs these functions?
explanation_steps: The nose, the lungs and the diaphragm are all used for breathing.
They belong to the respiratory system. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 11)
questions.explain_simple: Nose, lungs and diaphragm are breathing organs: the respiratory system.
tips: Respiratory system: nose, trachea, bronchi, lungs, diaphragm.

similar_questions.stem: Where does gas exchange happen in the lungs?
explanation_steps: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the alveoli.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the effect of unbalanced force?
explanation_steps: Unbalanced forces change the motion of an object: its position, speed or direction.
A force does not change the mass (amount of matter) of an object. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 52)
questions.explain_simple: A force can change speed and direction, but not mass.
tips: Unbalanced force → motion changes. Mass stays the same.

similar_questions.stem: A moving ball is stopped by a player's foot. What did the force change?
explanation_steps: The force changed its speed to zero.

questions.stem: The separation of white light into its colours is called
explanation_steps: When white light passes through a prism, it splits into seven colours. This splitting is called dispersion.
The band of colours produced is called a spectrum. Refraction is bending of light. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 75-76)
questions.explain_simple: Splitting white light into colours is dispersion.
tips: Dispersion = the splitting. Spectrum = the band of colours you see.

similar_questions.stem: A rainbow is formed when sunlight is dispersed by
explanation_steps: Raindrops act like tiny prisms and split sunlight into colours.

questions.stem: The diagram below shows a person rolling a barrel into the back of a truck. What simple machine is the person using to help roll the barrel?
questions.image_alt: A person pushes a barrel up a sloping board from the ground into the back of a truck.
explanation_steps: The person rolls the barrel up a sloping board (a ramp).
A sloping surface used to raise a load is an inclined plane. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 14)
questions.explain_simple: The sloping board is an inclined plane.
tips: Ramp = inclined plane.

similar_questions.stem: Which simple machine is an axe blade?
explanation_steps: Anything with a sharp edge that splits things is a wedge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not sexually transmitted disease?
explanation_steps: Gonorrhea, syphilis and AIDS are sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
A condom is not a disease at all. It is a rubber cover used during sex; it helps prevent pregnancy and STDs. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 193)
questions.explain_simple: A condom is not a disease. The other three are STDs.
tips: STDs in the book: gonorrhea, syphilis, AIDS.

similar_questions.stem: AIDS is caused by
explanation_steps: AIDS is caused by the HIV virus.

questions.stem: The type of blood cells that used in the clotting of blood are
explanation_steps: Platelets help blood to clot, so a cut stops bleeding.
Red blood cells carry oxygen; white blood cells fight germs; plasma is the liquid part. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 18)
questions.explain_simple: Platelets help blood clot.
tips: Red → oxygen. White → germs. Platelets → clotting.

similar_questions.stem: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
explanation_steps: Red blood cells carry oxygen.

questions.stem: One of the following is not true about sandy soil.

options.A: it has a coarse texture with large particles
options.B: it is classified as a light soil
options.C: it is difficult to dig and plough
options.D: its drainage and aeration are usually very fast

explanation_steps: Sandy soil has large particles, it is light, and water and air pass through it quickly.
The textbook says sandy soils are EASY to dig and plough. So C is not true. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Sandy soil is easy to dig. So C is wrong.
tips: Sandy: big particles, light, drains fast. Clay: tiny particles, heavy, holds water.

similar_questions.stem: Which soil holds the most water?
explanation_steps: Clay has very small particles and holds a lot of water.

questions.stem: Which human body system carries food and oxygen to the body tissues?
explanation_steps: The textbook says the circulatory system carries nutrients, oxygen and other useful substances to all the body cells.
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: The blood (circulatory system) carries food and oxygen to the body.
tips: Circulatory system: heart + blood vessels + blood.

similar_questions.stem: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
explanation_steps: The heart pumps blood.

questions.stem: The diagram below shows the percentage composition of air in the atmosphere. What does letter “y” represent?
explanation_steps: The key says Y = 21%.
Air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 1% other gases. So Y (21%) is oxygen. Answer: D.
(The pie chart itself is missing in the exam PDF, but the key is printed.)
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 86)
questions.explain_simple: Y is 21%. Oxygen makes up 21% of air.
tips: Air: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% other gases.

similar_questions.stem: In the same key, what is Z (78%)?
explanation_steps: 78% of air is nitrogen.

questions.stem: The motion that causes day and night is
explanation_steps: The earth rotates (spins) on its axis once in about 24 hours.
The side facing the sun has day; the other side has night. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 148)
questions.explain_simple: The earth spins. This makes day and night.
tips: Rotation → day and night. Revolution → year and seasons.

similar_questions.stem: The earth goes once around the sun in about
explanation_steps: One revolution takes about 365 days (one year).

questions.stem: The three main subatomic particles are
explanation_steps: An atom is made of three subatomic particles: protons, neutrons and electrons.
The nucleus and the shells are regions of the atom, not particles. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 74)
questions.explain_simple: Atoms are made of protons, neutrons and electrons.
tips: Proton (+), neutron (0), electron (−).

similar_questions.stem: Which two particles are found in the nucleus?
explanation_steps: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

questions.stem: Nearly three-quarter of the earth’s surface is covered by
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Water covers nearly three-quarters of the earth's surface.'
Dry land is only about one quarter. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Water covers about three quarters of the earth.
tips: Earth's surface: about 3/4 water, 1/4 land.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the earth's water is found in
explanation_steps: Over 97% of the earth's water is in the oceans and seas.

questions.stem: Which of the following natural resources is not renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Oil is a fossil fuel. Once used, it cannot be replaced, so it is non-renewable.
Soil, air and water can be renewed. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 62)
questions.explain_simple: Oil is non-renewable. It cannot be made again quickly.
tips: Fossil fuels = non-renewable.

similar_questions.stem: Which is non-renewable?
explanation_steps: Coal is a fossil fuel, so it is non-renewable.

questions.stem: The diagram below shows a food chain. Which organisms in this food chain are herbivores?
questions.image_alt: Food chain: the sun shines on green plants → grasshopper → birds → snakes.
explanation_steps: A herbivore eats only plants.
In the chain green plants → grasshopper → birds → snakes, the grasshopper eats the green plants.
Green plants are producers; birds and snakes eat animals (carnivores). Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 126)
questions.explain_simple: Grasshoppers eat plants, so they are herbivores.
tips: The animal right after the plant in a food chain is the herbivore.

similar_questions.stem: In the same food chain, which organism is the top carnivore?
explanation_steps: Snakes are at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a way of heat transfer?
explanation_steps: Heat transfers in three ways: conduction, convection and radiation.
Specific heat is a property of a material (how much heat it needs to warm up). It is not a way of heat transfer. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 105)
questions.explain_simple: Specific heat is not a way that heat moves.
tips: Heat moves by conduction, convection, radiation.

similar_questions.stem: Heat moves through a metal spoon in hot tea by
explanation_steps: In solids, heat moves by conduction.

questions.stem: Identify the correct pathway of nerve impulse.

options.A: Response → Receptor → Control center → Effector → Stimulus
options.B: Effector → Receptor → Response → Stimulus → Control center
options.C: Stimulus → Receptor → Control center → Effector → Response
options.D: Receptor → Stimulus → Control center → Effector → Response

explanation_steps: First comes the stimulus (a change). A receptor detects it.
The message goes to the control centre (brain or spinal cord), then to an effector (muscle or gland), which makes the response. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 131)
questions.explain_simple: Stimulus → receptor → control centre → effector → response.
tips: Change → sense → decide → act → result.

similar_questions.stem: You touch a hot pan and pull your hand away. The heat of the pan is the
explanation_steps: The heat is the change that starts the pathway: the stimulus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct chemical symbol of an element?
explanation_steps: Rule: the first letter is a capital letter and the second letter is small.
'ne' and 'mG' start with a small letter; 'NA' has a capital second letter. Only Al (aluminium) is correct. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 85)
questions.explain_simple: Al is written correctly: capital A, small l.
tips: First letter BIG, second letter small.

similar_questions.stem: How should the symbol of magnesium be written?
explanation_steps: Capital M, small g: Mg.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: The table below shows four different atoms and their number of electrons and electronic structure. Based on the table, which atom has greater number of electrons in its last shell?
explanation_steps: The last number in the electronic structure is the number of electrons in the last shell.
W has the most electrons in its last shell (8). Answer: D. (Do not choose Z just because it has the most electrons in total.)
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 78)
questions.explain_simple: W (2, 8) has 8 electrons in its last shell. That is the most.
tips: Last shell = last number in the electronic structure.

similar_questions.stem: An atom has the structure 2, 8, 3. How many electrons are in its last shell?
explanation_steps: The last number is 3.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about asexual reproduction?

options.B: it is a slow way of producing new individuals
options.C: all the new individuals produced are the same as their parents
options.D: two parents of opposite sex are needed for asexual reproduction

explanation_steps: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent.
The textbook says all the new individuals produced asexually are the same as their parent and each other.
It happens in animals too (e.g. Hydra budding), it is fast, and it does not need two parents. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: In asexual reproduction the young are copies of the one parent.
tips: Asexual: one parent, fast, copies. Sexual: two parents, variety.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an example of asexual reproduction?

options.B: a potato growing new plants from its buds
options.D: a cow giving birth after mating

explanation_steps: New potato plants grow from buds of one parent: asexual.

questions.stem: Pesticides that kill weeds are known as
explanation_steps: Herbicides control (kill) weeds.
Insecticides kill insects, rodenticides kill rats and mice, fungicides kill fungi. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 192)
questions.explain_simple: Herbicides kill weeds.
tips: herbi = plants, insecti = insects, rodenti = rats.

similar_questions.stem: A farmer's crops have a fungus disease. Which pesticide should he use?
explanation_steps: Fungicides kill fungi.

questions.stem: An incomplete electric circuit is shown below. The lightbulb is not giving light. Which object placed at “X” would complete the circuit and light the bulb?
questions.image_alt: A lightbulb connected by a wire along the top and a wire along the bottom. On the right side there is a gap marked X. There is no battery in the drawing.
explanation_steps: Look at the circuit: it has a bulb and wires, but NO battery (no cell). Without a source of electricity, no current can flow.
A metal nail would only close the gap; with no battery the bulb still would not light. A switch or a second bulb also gives no electricity.
Only a battery at X both completes the circuit and gives the energy to light the bulb. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 161)
questions.explain_simple: The circuit has no battery. Put a battery at X and the bulb will light.
tips: A working circuit needs: a source (cell/battery), wires, a load (bulb), and a closed path.

similar_questions.stem: Which material will let current flow if it is put in a gap in a circuit?
explanation_steps: Copper is a metal and a good conductor of electricity.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Introduction to Electricity and Magnetism

questions.stem: The increase in average temperature of the earth because of the keeping heat by gases released to the atmosphere is known as____.
explanation_steps: This is the textbook's definition of global warming.
Gases like carbon dioxide keep heat in the air, so the earth becomes warmer. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Gases keep heat in the air. The earth gets warmer. This is global warming.
tips: More CO₂ → more heat kept → global warming.

similar_questions.stem: What may happen if global warming continues?
explanation_steps: Warmer temperatures melt polar ice, so sea level rises.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 9 – Human Impact on the Environment

questions.stem: Any material that causes pollution in the environment is called
explanation_steps: A pollutant is a harmful substance that pollutes the environment.
Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 189)
questions.explain_simple: Anything that pollutes is a pollutant.
tips: Pollution = the harm. Pollutant = the thing that causes it.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an air pollutant?
explanation_steps: Smoke from cars pollutes the air.

questions.stem: Plant response that involves movement toward and away from the stimulus is
explanation_steps: A tropism is a growth movement of a plant towards (positive) or away from (negative) a stimulus.
A nastic movement does not depend on the direction of the stimulus (e.g. flowers opening in the morning). Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 80)
questions.explain_simple: Moving toward or away from a stimulus is a tropism.
tips: Tropism: direction matters. Nastic: direction does not matter.

similar_questions.stem: A shoot bends towards a window. This is
explanation_steps: It grows towards light: positive phototropism.

questions.stem: A reflected sound is called
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A reflected sound is called an echo.'
Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A sound that bounces back is an echo.
tips: Echo = reflection of sound.

similar_questions.stem: You shout near a big cliff and hear your voice again. What do you hear?
explanation_steps: The sound reflects from the cliff: an echo.

questions.stem: The figure below shows one of the types of breeze. Which type of breeze is shown?
questions.image_alt: Night: land (cool) on the left, sea (warm) on the right. Warm air rises over the sea, moves over the top to the land, and cool air flows along the bottom from the land to the sea.
explanation_steps: The figure is at night. The land is cool and the sea is warm.
Warm air rises over the sea, and cool air moves from the land to the sea (arrows at the bottom).
Cool air blowing from the land to the sea at night is a land breeze. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 109)
questions.explain_simple: At night cool air moves from the land to the sea. This is a land breeze.
tips: Day: sea breeze (sea → land). Night: land breeze (land → sea).

similar_questions.stem: During a hot day near the coast, the breeze blows
explanation_steps: In the day the land is warmer, so cool air moves from the sea to the land.

questions.stem: The speed of sound in air is 330 m/s. How far will sound travel through air in 20 seconds?
explanation_steps: Distance = speed × time.
330 m/s × 20 s = 6600 m. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208)
tips: distance = speed × time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an acquired trait?
explanation_steps: An acquired trait is gained during life, not from genes.
A scar comes from an injury. It is acquired. Skin colour, height and eye colour are inherited. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 142)
questions.explain_simple: A scar comes from an injury during life. It is acquired.
tips: Inherited = from genes. Acquired = from life events.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an inherited trait?
explanation_steps: Eye colour comes from the parents' genes.

questions.stem: The table below shows specific heat of aluminum, lead, iron and copper. If the same amounts of heat were added to equal masses of these substances, which substance will be the hottest?
explanation_steps: Specific heat is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K.
A substance with a SMALL specific heat heats up fastest.
Lead has the smallest specific heat (130 J/(kg K)), so with the same heat it becomes the hottest. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 126; Science Grade 8, p. 130)
questions.explain_simple: Lead has the lowest specific heat, so it gets hot fastest.
tips: Low specific heat → heats fast. High specific heat → heats slowly.

similar_questions.stem: Water has a high specific heat. This means water
explanation_steps: A high specific heat means much heat is needed, so water heats slowly.
